From George Till, CUMBRIA

Dear Mr. Cavers,

I wonder if you will help me
please with a difficulty that I
am experiencing in printing text
on A4 tractor feed paper with my
M-1009 Brother printer and TW3.

The printer has the options of
10" or 11" form length on the
dipswitches and when the pages
are numbered at the top I find
that if A4 paper is used (which
is about 11. 6" long) if the 0"
option is used I get two numbers
on the one sheet. If 11" is
chosen the numbers on the top
are printed futher down the
sheet as more sheets are printed

until, at about the 7th or 8th
sheet, the sheet number has come
down noticeably from the top of
the sheet. this seems to happen
no matter how many lines on
page are chosen from the customs
option or whether the automatic
page break or forced feed symbol
is used. Can you tell me please
what I am overlooking?

   Best wishes and thank you,

           George Till

To George Till from Brian Cavers


The problem arises because you
are using "true A4" rather than
the "standard" printer size. A
year or two ago I bought a pack
of the size you are now using
and it was nothing but trouble.
So, the ultimate solution is to
buy "standard" 11" printer paper
in the future.

Meanwhile,I can only suggest the
following: Study Page 50 of your
TW3 manual and you'll see how to
redefine a printer graphic for a
particular sequence of printer
codes. Select one you don't use
regularly and alter the codes to
67,72.

You will then need to use this
graphic at the top of each docu-
ment when typing in TW3. If it's
a nuisance you might consider a
pre-loader BASIC program with...
10 LPRINT CHR$ 67;CHR$ 72
20 LOAD "TW3"   ...but this will
depend on where (or if) your
printer is initialized elsewhere
and set up your interface first
to send control codes (e.g. for
Disciple, POKE @6,1).

The 72 is the number of lines it
should give you per sheet. I had
to guess at 72 but I don't think
it's far out. You will need to
experiment - adjusting it down
to 71 or 70 or up to 73 or 74
until your print-outs are right.
Let me know how you get on. -BC.

From: Raymond Hoy, BASINGSTOKE

Can you, or any one out there,
tell me what is the most cost
effective and best way to go
about connecting a second drive
to my Disciple?  Where do I
get a compatible drive and the
right lead to connect it to what
I already have?

I know a lead can be obtained
from a company called WATFORD
ELECTRONICS (see below for full
address). This lead(or six conn-
ector) is wired up in such a way
that you don't have to alter
either of the drives to say
which is drive 1 or 2. It costs
`12.00.I know I've answered some
of the question but a second
opinion can't do any harm.

WATFORD ELECTRONICS
JESSA HOUSE
250 LOWER HIGH STREET
WATFORD
HERTFORDSHIRE
WD1 2AN        Tel: 0923 3774

May I at this point ask you and
your readers if any one knows of
a simple accounting program. The
type I need is input expenses in
different catagories. Each
catagory to have a total and an
income catogory. Inputs must be
able to be altered and deleted.
The program I use at the moment
was typed from INPUT and does
not allow you to delete an input
only alter it which can be very
annoying sometimes. Plus it only
allows me to enter 200 entries
which is now no good to me.

Print options are a must. Maybe
the one below is what I need.

May I suggest for OUTLET EXTRA 2
'CLIP COMPOSER', 'FINANCE
MANAGER' and 'EXPENSHEET'.

     Keep up the good work.

           Raymond Hoy

To Raymond Hoy from Brian Gaff

I must admit I always try to set
the 2nd drive I use internally
and I have thus never used the
cable you mention.I suspect how-
ever,you will still have to open
the drives to plug the cable in,
as adding too much extra cable
could affect reliability.

I am told some PC drive doubler
cables can often be used for
this purpose, and generally only
cost half of what you mention,so
it may be worth shopping around.

They achieve the drive switching
by having a twist in some wires
of the ribbon cable to fool the
machine into thinking the drive
has had its jumpers altered.

Really, I can only advise you to
make sure the connectors are of
the header type and of the right
sex for your drives!

Accounting programs are not my
forte, but I seem to recall one
called EXPEND in a previous
issue of OUTLET. This may not be
what you want, but apart from
full blown Spreadsheets like
TASCALC, there is nothing I can
suggest.Maybe one of our readers
has something that can help you?
                         - B.G.

[EXPEND sounds familiar but I
couldn't track it down! However,
I think EXPENSHEET (OUTLET 12)is
the nearest we can get. I use it
every month but it only has one
total.                   -B.C.]

From: Mike Haine, LEAMINGTON

DEAR EDS,

I see there has been further
query about the possibility of
getting together the various
items for improving Tasword 2 in
an effort to produce the 'ideal'
version.  I think this is a
splendid idea.

I further think it should be
extended to other programs e.g.,
assemblers etc.

I suggest that there is room for
much more user discussion on
such facilities, particularly
for suggestions and critical
comment to inspire the program
writers.

Tasword 2 is a particularly
useful program in that all the
important parts requiring fast
operation are in MACHINE CODE;
while the control system, menus
etc, are in BASIC. This makes it
especially easy to modify. I
have just sent off a bit of
BASIC to OUTLET which can be
merged into TASWORD 2(SAM COUPE)
version to give the option of
printing the text-file in two 64
character columns. I also have a
few other mods to improve the
operation such as pop-up menus,
simpler LOAD and SAVE. I am
happy to make these available to
anyone who cares to send me a
tape or disc with a SAE (and
perhaps a stamp for the 'SAVE
THE CHILDREN CHARITY'.

If you have any suggestions
for other improvements do write.
(see address at end).

Re: Someone's query on radio:
The 1991 "The WORLD RADIO TV
HANDBOOK" gives comprehensive
country by country,listings of
long, medium and short wave
broadcasters by frequency time
and language.

  PW publishing Ltd. The Quay,
    Poole, Dorset, BH15 1PP

developed a new colour ink jet
printhead that should bring four
colour printing within the

businesses! Piezoelectric (PZT)

of ink, each 0.04 microlitres in
volume. Print speed of 60 pages
per minute possible!!!!!!

Mike Haine,Riverside,Welsh Rd.,
OFFCHURCH,LEAMINGTON,CV33 9AH.




Many thanks, Mike.
                        - Brian

From: Paul Preston,
100 Trelawney Rd, Hainault,
ILFORD, Essex 1GG 2NW

The system I am using is a 128k
Sinclair Spectrum Opus Discovery
(ROM 2.2 and RAM chip) and
Multiface 128.

A recent project I've been work-
ing on requires a lot of files
to be placed in RAM disk 5. The
normal catalogue allocation only
allows 14 files. Now on page 28
of the Opus manual in section 6
"The catalogue file" is a way of
expanding the catalogue.

This doesn't work and the syntax
is also wrong as after "CAT"
must follow a semi-colon and the
drive number.

  OPEN# 4;"CAT";5EXP 1024
  CLEAR #4

I have included a short program
"OPUSPROB" to illustrate this.
Run the program then CAT 5.
Delete just the REM in line 20
and then RUN followed by CAT 5.

I wonder if you or any readers
can help or is this a bug?

Does anyone have more inform-
ation on the Opus Discovery jump
tables? In particular the direct
file manipulation table 14H. As
a member of the S.D.C. I already
have the excellent issue 4
describing how to use most jump
tables but not 14H. Is there an
Opus R.O.M. disassembly?

Can anyone tell me how to set
the letter header option in
Tasword 2 (it's driving me mad!)
This is after Tasword has been
modified by TAS-EXTRAS in Outlet
24.  When I go through the
sequence 1, 2 and 3 all I get is
blank lines inserted even if I
type my address at stage 2.There
appears to be no full descript-
ion of how to use this feature
in the Drivechat article.

         Yours sincerely,

          Paul Preston

Brian Cavers to Paul Preston

The RAMDISK problem does seem to
be a bug. I couldn't get it to
work.DRIVECHAT (pp.15 to 17) has
info on Table 14H but it may be
what you already have.There's no
published Opus ROM disassembly.
I'd SAVE CODE 0,16383 and print
a disassembly- no comments but
better than nothing! Have you a
disassembler?

The TAS-EXTRAS letterhead option
is badly described. First choose
Option 2, type your header then
exit.Use Option 1 to SET the new
header. Delete the text so you
have a clear page to test on and
exit again.Press 3 to insert the
header then resave the code.
                        - Brian

From: Derek Morgan, 18 Mill Lane
Glenburn Road, Old Skelmersdale,
Lancashire. WN8 8RH

Hi Brian, Ron,

Many thanks for Issue 42, it's
great. It's even better than
usual because it has two little
programs in Addenders by me.
Thanks for printing them and
even more thanks for the cheque.

My wife sealed up and posted my
disc for Issue 42 before my
letter to you was finished so I
will have another go at saying
thanks for LISTFORMAT3. It makes
programming a lot easier. I was
very disappointed not to find
it as part of SAM BASIC.

I read with interest the letter
from bilge pump assistant, Mike
Pike, when he let slip that Bob
Smith was none other than the
famous Bos'un Bob of Buccaneer
fame. He goes on to say the
curiosity was killing him, no
doubt Bob will lend him a hand.

I look back with fondest memory
of the days of BUCCANEER where
anything went and we all learned
a lot. I wonder if Issue 44 will
bring forward the revelation
that our own editors, Ron and
Brian were once deckhands on the
good ship BUCCANEER. I live in
fear that I'll be recognised and
one day it will be printed in
OUTLET that I've been recognised
as none other than the infamous
Morgan the Pirate.

Are there any more buccaneers
out there?

I'm having problems getting
'Lords of Midnight' to run on
Sam through Samtape 3. It loads
and runs O.K. until you go into
night mode, and then it locks
up.

If you have it up and running,
then please get in touch (3.5"
disc).

I've been trying to slow down
the auto repeat key on the Sam
version of PCG's DTP. I have
tried poking SVAR's 512 and 522,
but this has no affect. Yes!, I
have written to PCG, but my
letter has not been replied to.

The Sam mouse is scheduled for
release around March/April at a
proposed retail price of `35.00.

There are no longer any plans
for a 'Lords of Midnight' and
'Doomdarks Revenge' on Sam
format.

If any member has any problems
getting the Tasword2 (Samtape)
help pages in Outlet 42 working,
then please get in touch.

Will Outlet be able to work with
Masterdos in the future?.

             Yours,

              Derek

Brian Cavers to Derek Morgan

I reckon the informal, humorous
atmosphere of BUCCANEER must
have had its influence on OUTLET
although we run a tighter ship!
Yes, you've been recognized you
swab and serve you right if your
auto repeat key accelerates into
orbit.No wonder PCG didn't reply
- probably couldn't read your
magenta letter paper.I'll get my
own back by putting this reply
on PAPER 3! Ha! The key problem
sounds like a very heavy hacking
job.SC_ASSEMBLER and TASWORD had
the same problem to start with.

I do have a solution for LOM. If
it locks up in night mode then
only play it during the day.

OUTLET already can be run under
MASTERDOS which is downwardly
compatible - that is, it loads
files saved under SAMdos. If you
mean files be saved in OUTLET in
Masterdos sub-directories then
no - because not everyone has
Masterdos so will not be able to
access them. If you mean will
Masterdos be the DOS on the disc
then also no; it's a copyrighted
program and cannot be copied to
other people. If however, you
mean will we be publishing any
programs that specifically use
the extra Masterdos features,for
example, a database that uses
opentype files then, yes - if
readers contribute such programs
they will be considered for
publication.         - Brian

From: Mike Pike, NORTHALLERTON

Thanks for your advice about
word processor formats in OUTLET
issue 042.

I gave up the idea of program-
ming my own WP software when I
found a brand new copy of 'The
Writer' for `5.99.It's not ideal
but perhaps that's because I'm
used to using my PC at work.

One grumble I have about it is
the tape file format used. It
consists of a standard code
block header, followed by some
data (presumably containing the
document settings like tabs,
etc.) immediately followed by a
headerless block containing the
ASCII text.

This certainly makes things
difficult for importing text
into your own programs. E.G. my
parallel printer interface
(constructed from an article in
Everyday Electronics) requires
direct control from the micro,
i.e.the Spectrum must handle the
control lines, set and reset the
strobe line, etc. by use of IN &
OUT instructions.

I have a printer buffer resident
program which allows the use of
LPRINT and a program which
performs similar to 'COPY' both
outputting to an Epson printer.

However, as 'The Writer' doesn't
support the ZX Printer, I have
to write my own printer program
for 'Writer' files.

This is obviously going to pose
problems with the loading of the
headerless block.

At the moment,I'll have to use a
byte counter(as used in the Lerm
TC7 tape copier) to measure the
length of the block then make up
a false header. 'The Writer' can
print through Interface 1(RS232)
Kempston, Hilderbay K, H and T
and Euroelectronics interfaces.

Is there any way I can use any
of these, e.g. by altering the
addresses used for my interface
through hardware?

Probably the easiest way is to
buy a new interface and a copy
of Tasword, but I'd like to make


the most of what I've got.  Any
info gratefully received! I know
that it is difficult to make
modifications to 'The Writer'
because it's written in m/c, but
is there something I could try?

I am put off buying microdrives
because I have heard stories of
them being unreliable and that
cartridges are no longer being
manufactured. Can you clear this
up for me?.

To Mike Pike from Brian Cavers

Try using SAMBYTES (OUTLET 39)to
load the headerless tape files.
This is designed to ignore the
first header it comes across so
it may work if you start the
tape just past the first part of
the first header so that it will
pick up the second part of the
first header (but discard it)and
then load the headerless file.
Otherwise, try loading the first
part of the first header then
skip the second part (turn down
the volume for a few seconds?)
then load the headerless block.

This may be as messy as making
up a false header as you said so
it may not be of much use!

I think hacking into the printer
routines in THE WRITER would be
a major job. Best of luck unless
anyone can suggest anything.

Yes, microdrive cartridges are
very unreliable and expensive
compared to other media such as
3.5" discs. Furthermore,they are
not being manufactured anymore.
The existing stocks seem to be
increasing in price and, as we
warned quite a while ago, it can
only be a matter of time until
even OUTLET becomes impractical
to sustain on the system. Our
present supply has recently
dried up and we must now pay too
high a price to be practical for
long. I recommend anyone using
microdrives to upgrade to a +D
disc drive system.      - Brian

From: Tony Catts

My skill at Computing is NIL. I
use the simplest of programs (on
A GOTO!) To access the infor-
mation I store and use M/tape.
The system is compact and easy
to carry about. The M/tape boxes
are easily stacked and the end
info read. I have something like
130 tapes which are often in use
(not counting OUTLET).

In the past, I have had the disc
versions from you up to Issue 35
but my two systems do not
communicate. How does one get
info from Disc to M/drive??? Can
one?

      Many thanks. Cheers, Tony

To Tony Catts from Brian Cavers

I don't have to hand which drive
system you are using.If Disciple
then Interface 1 can be attached
piggy-back fashion. Press the
back button;use OUT 31,16 before
loading files from disc and OUT
31,0 before saving on micro-
drive. Failing that the only
option is to save files on tape
and reload in the microdrive.

You need some skill to do this
as there are so many potential
problems it would take a book to
explain! OUTLET will not run
correctly on the wrong system.It
takes me days to convert OUTLET
for all systems EVERY MONTH! -
                        - Brian

From: Malcolm Goodman, LEEDS

Dear Ron and Brian,

Have just returned from three
brilliant weeks holidays in the
U.S.A. I visited San Francisco,
Los Angeles, Las Vegas, Salt
Lake City, Orlando and Miami.
Not a sign of 8 bits anywhere.
How backward can you get?

One small comment that I keep
meaning to mention. When I store
my disks I do so with the metal
cover at the bottom. As a result
your label finishes upside down
and I have to peel it off and
re-fix it. Am I alone in this
feeling? Perhaps you might care
to ask your other readers.

In answer to your query in
Outlet No.043 about disabling
the VERIFY when FORMATTING, I
discovered that on the +D the
command FORMAT D1 to 0 seemed to
do what you seek. I can only
suggest that you try it on the
Disciple.

          Kind Regards,

         Malcolm Goodman

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Goodman

Thanks, Malcolm. It's all right
for some ain't it?While you were
lazing in Miami some of us were
slavin' over a hot keyboard to
get OUTLET ready in time for
your return.

This disc label double-standard
is a pain. It seems that nothing
can be invented without varying
conventions bodging things up. I
wonder what percentage of people
label discs in one direction to
the other? Both methods are very
common. Perhaps a two-way label,
like a playing card, is the way?

Thanks for the FORMAT tip though
I need one without an error at
the end.                - Brian

From: Jim Hossack, WEST KILBRIDE

With regard to Outlet No. 013,
I've one small problem. The
machine-code article is fasc-
inating;it's pitched at just the
right level for me. However,
I've had some trouble printing
"Outclass" to disk (I have the
+3), but there is, of course, no
+3 print command. According to
the +3 handbook, there is no
chance of using a printer in the
"48k mode" of this machine.

I discovered that by entering
the "ZX printer" option I was
able to copy each screen of the
"Outclass" text to print, but
apart from being very slow, this
"copy" method goes through
ribbons like a dose of salts!

What I wondered was, do you have
a ready-made text, possibly of
the whole of your machine-code
course which I could buy and
read like a book. Or maybe you
do publish it as a book?

I have the same problem with the
'Speclist' but it doesn't bother
me there as I only need to print
out the occasional page. Rather
surprisingly, the "Outstart"
disassembler, when transferred
to disk and used on the +3, does
a perfect job of printing out
the machine code instructions!
(This when used with the "ZX
printer" option.

By the way, my printer is the
Panasonic KX-P1081).

On the subject of printing, my
"Tasword 2" word-processer did
not print out when used with the
+3, in fact I didn't expect it
to, as I'd been warned that I'd
need to buy the Tasword 3 to
work with this computer.

However, not feeling like fork-
ing out another `25.00, I exp-
erimented a bit, and added a
BASIC LPRINT program, using the
text stored at 32000 onwards.
It works, if a bit slowly. I
feel there ought to be a fairly
simple mod to the machine-code
which should enable it to print
without the use of BASIC. Please
let me know if I'm right but
DON'T tell me what it is as I'd
like to figure it out myself.

Finally, I'd just like to say
that I stumbled upon your
address by chance, never having
seen any adverts. Have you
considered advertising in the
Amateur Radio mags - there must
be an enormous number of serious
Spectrum users in this field?

     73's and all the best,

           Jim Hossack

Brian Cavers to Jim Hossack


Thanks, Jim. We have considered
promotion in magazines other
than the general computer media,
e.g., electronics periodicals.We
shall certainly think also of
amateur radio magazines when we
have more resources to expend on
our meagre advertising budget.

There's a +3 print option in the
+3 version of OUTLET. I assume
you take the tape version? Why
not treat yourself to one issue
of OUTLET on +3 disc? Load it,
switch in the disc on which you
have saved OUTCLASS,load it in
(must be filename: "OUTCLASS.#")
and then print it.

Alternatively, just BREAK into
your present version and enter:
 1420 FORMAT LPRINT "U": RETURN
Run the program and select the
LPRINT III option to print. You
can resave the program with the
change by entering RUN 9983.

I think OUTSTART does not send
any printer codes but merely
uses LPRINT which, of course, is
the same for all systems.

Sorry, we do not sell any OUTLET
text articles in hard copy form.

I'm puzzled about your problem
with Tasword 2 on a +3. I can't
think why printout doesn't work.
Has anyone got it working?
                         -Brian

From: Kenneth Stearn, FIFE

Dear Sir,

I am thinking of upgrading and
am swithering between a Sam
Coupe and extending my existing
set up with a +D or Disciple.

At the moment, I have a Plus 2
(grey), interface 1 and one
microdrive. This has attached, a
Kempston E Centronics Interface
controlling a Toshiba 24-dot
Expresswriter 301.

When talking about a Plus D,does
that mean an interface, or does
this include the disk drive and
interface? Where could I buy it
and what kind of price range?

Also if I bought a Sam Coupe,
what drive system does it have
and will my printer and inter-
face be compatible?

I would be interested in your
comments.

         Kenneth Stearn

Brian Cavers to Kenneth Stearn

"Swithering" -that's a good old-
fashioned-sounding word is it
not? It sent me scurrying for my
trusty dictionary!

The Plus D is a drive INTERFACE
but is available with a drive at
just `129.99(`59.99 without)from
Datel Electronics Ltd. Govan Rd.
Fenton Industrial Estate,Fenton,
Stoke-on-Trent, ST4 2RS (Tel:
0782 744707). It will work with
your printer but you will need a
BBC-type lead which Datel sell
at `9.99.

Yes, your printer will also work
with SAM but you will need to
buy an additional printer inter-
face for `29.95.

The SAM COUPE is supplied with a
3.5" double-density,double-sided
drive which gives 780K of space,
the same format as the +D. It's
`199.95 from SAM COMPUTERS LTD.,
Lakeside, Phoenix Way, Swansea
Enterprise Park, Swansea SA7 9EH
(Tel: 0792 700300). The printer
interface needs a BBC-type conn-
ector like the +D and I'm not
sure that SAMCO do them BUT, If
you decide to go for a SAM and
don't already have the BBC-type
lead you can order SAM, printer
Interface (same price as SAMCO)
AND LEAD (`7.99) from SAMCO's
authorised repair shop: PBT
ELECTRONICS LTD.,Port Talbot
Workshops, Unit 17,Addison Road,
Port Talbot, SA12 6HZ (Tel: 0639
885008).
                        - Brian.

From George Till, CUMBRIA

Dear Mr. Cavers,

I wonder if you will help me please with a difficulty that I am experiencing in printing text on A4 tractor feed paper with my M-1009 Brother printer and TW3.

The printer has the options of 10" or 11" form length on the dipswitches and when the pages are numbered at the top I find that if A4 paper is used (which is about 11. 6" long) if the 0" option is used I get two numbers on the one sheet. If 11" is chosen the numbers on the top are printed futher down the sheet as more sheets are printed

until, at about the 7th or 8th sheet, the sheet number has come down noticeably from the top of the sheet. this seems to happen no matter how many lines on page are chosen from the customs option or whether the automatic page break or forced feed symbol is used. Can you tell me please what I am overlooking?

Best wishes and thank you,

George Till

To George Till from Brian Cavers

The problem arises because you are using "true A4" rather than the "standard" printer size. A year or two ago I bought a pack of the size you are now using and it was nothing but trouble. So, the ultimate solution is to buy "standard" 11" printer paper in the future.

Meanwhile,I can only suggest the following: Study Page 50 of your TW3 manual and you'll see how to redefine a printer graphic for a particular sequence of printer codes. Select one you don't use regularly and alter the codes to 67,72.

You will then need to use this graphic at the top of each docu- ment when typing in TW3. If it's a nuisance you might consider a pre-loader BASIC program with... 10 LPRINT CHR$ 67;CHR$ 72 20 LOAD "TW3"   ...but this will depend on where (or if) your printer is initialized elsewhere and set up your interface first to send control codes (e.g. for Disciple, POKE @6,1).

The 72 is the number of lines it should give you per sheet. I had to guess at 72 but I don't think it's far out. You will need to experiment - adjusting it down to 71 or 70 or up to 73 or 74 until your print-outs are right. Let me know how you get on. -BC.

### George Till от Brian Cavers

Проблема возникает из-за того, что вы используете «настоящий A4», а не «стандартный» для принтеров размер. Пару лет назад я купил пачку бумаги того формата, что вы используете сейчас, и с ней были сплошные неприятности. Так что кардинальное решение — покупать в будущем «стандартную» 11-дюймовую бумагу для принтера.

Пока же я могу лишь предложить следующее: изучите страницу 50 руководства к TW3, и вы увидите, как переопределить графический символ принтера для определенной последовательности управляющих кодов. Выберите тот, который вы обычно не используете, и измените коды на 67, 72.

Затем вам нужно будет ставить этот символ в самом верху каждого документа при наборе в TW3. Если это утомительно, можете рассмотреть вариант загрузочной BASIC-программы:

```basic
10 LPRINT CHR$ 67;CHR$ 72
20 LOAD "TW3"
```
